beats.say: The release reviewer signs for candidate C seventeen at ten percent. The evaluation note contains an untrusted instruction. Under policy G seven, that instruction requires a security signature. Look at the security line. Can the rollout go ahead?

Hold the rollout. Security still has to sign. Now open the executor record. The trace stays flat. Zero traffic changes. The owner can challenge the hold if a signature was missed. A reviewer who took no part in the decision checks the original request, policy and receipts, then adds the reason to the file.

Who could a bad rollout hurt? The workflow map names the people who will use the new model. Measure what happened on both unauthorized and legitimate requests. Manage the risk by holding an unsafe change or repairing a mistaken denial. The release owner decides who can accept the remaining risk.

These are the four functions in NIST's voluntary AI Risk Management Framework. Govern applies throughout Map, Measure and Manage. As of late twenty twenty-six, version one is under revision. The Generative AI Profile covers risks including harmful outputs, information integrity, privacy and security.

ISO forty-two thousand and one uses Plan, Do, Check, Act for an organization's AI management system. Apply that cycle here. Plan the approval rule, run the gate, check its denials, then repair the gate if it missed a valid receipt. Each release still needs its own safety evidence and legal review.

title: Review follows the workflow and the people it affects

beats.say: Three requests arrive for the same model. One summarizes public documents, one helps assess a loan applicant, and one proposes a production change. Follow the effect to the person who bears it. Check the four intake fields. Which request goes to specialized risk review?

The credit application goes first to specialized risk review. The promotion assistant needs interaction and effect review. With all four flags checked false, public summarization takes the baseline route. These are engineering routes. Qualified reviewers determine legal status from the jurisdiction, the actor's role and the intended use.

Now erase the summarizer's worker-management answer. Where does that file go? To facts review. An unanswered field has priority even when the other answers are known. Record who established the facts and when the legal basis was checked. Replacing a model also calls for another look at the workflow.

title: Classify the workflow and identify each actor

beats.say: Begin the EU assessment with territorial scope and actor role. Article two includes providers placing systems or general-purpose models on the Union market, EU deployers, and certain non-EU providers and deployers where system output is used in the Union.

Trace the output of a credit application to the lender using it in the Union. Record the intended decision, people affected, market and actor. This file uses the amended text checked on November sixth, twenty twenty-six. A launch needs a dated classification and qualified signoff.
An application developer can be the provider of an AI system even when another organization supplies its general-purpose model.

A provider develops an AI system or a general-purpose AI model, or has it developed. Under its own name or trademark, it can place either one on the market. For an AI system, putting it into service under that name or trademark is another route. The lender uses the credit system under its authority. That makes it the deployer here.
A credit application can be a high-risk system built on a general-purpose model with separate model-provider duties.

The four-level intake map asks about prohibited practices, high-risk systems, particular transparency duties, and minimal or no risk. A high-risk assistant can also have transparency obligations. The local triage checks unknown facts first, then credit or worker management, then direct interaction or executable effects, then baseline.

Try the staff scheduler. It manages workers and talks to people. The other two fields are checked false. Worker management takes priority, so send it to specialized risk review. Change a checked answer to unknown and the file goes to facts review first. A qualified reviewer takes it from there.

title: A prohibited-use screen needs conditions and exceptions

beats.say: Screen for prohibited practices before release review. Article five covers specified techniques that manipulate people or exploit their vulnerabilities. Check how the system materially distorts behavior and whether it causes significant harm or is reasonably likely to do so. Now follow a social score. A sports club uses AI to rate a member's conduct at games over a season. A housing office receives the score. What did the office do with it?

It denied the member housing because of the club score. That ties data collected at games to adverse treatment in an unrelated setting. Article five also covers adverse treatment that's unjustified or disproportionate to the person's social behavior or its seriousness. Record the source of the score and the housing denial together. Stop this prohibited use before release.

Article five covers untargeted facial-image scraping to build or expand recognition databases and certain sensitive biometric classifications. For individual criminal-risk prediction, ask whether it relies solely on profiling or personality traits. Does the system support a human assessment of this person's involvement in criminal activity? The assessor must already have objective, verifiable facts directly linked to that activity.

Consider a tool that infers a person's emotions at work or in education. What input does it use? This prohibition concerns inference from biometric data, such as measurements from a person's face. Check the intended use and whether the tool is for a medical or safety reason.

For law enforcement, real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces is prohibited except for strictly necessary uses serving listed objectives. Those include finding a missing person or a specified victim, preventing certain serious threats and locating certain serious-offence suspects. Take a targeted missing-person search. On this form, which line can we check from the purpose alone?

That establishes the listed objective. What evidence shows that real-time identification is strictly necessary for this search? Could a less intrusive method find the person in time? Weigh the harm of delay against the impact on others. Check the limits on people, area and time, and the applicable authorization. Hold this request. The file gives us the purpose, but no justification for this use or evidence of those safeguards.

The July amendment covers nonconsensual intimate material and child sexual abuse material from December second, twenty twenty-six. For a provider, ask whether generating or manipulating this material is the system's purpose. A second route covers a reasonably foreseeable, reproducible outcome without significant technical modification if the system lacks adequate safeguards to prevent it and correct misuse. For a deployer, ask whether generating or manipulating it is the purpose of the use.

Read the definitions for the material and conduct in question. The child sexual abuse material provision includes a condition for a defence under national law. Record the legal basis, decision and date for the actual use.

title: Follow both high-risk routes and test the exception

beats.say: Article six has two high-risk routes. For the product route, consider software in an Annex one product. Which job does it do? A display that only makes the interface more convenient has no safety function in our example. Check both the product or safety-component criterion and the relevant third-party health and safety assessment.

Replace the display module with a cut-off that prevents overheating. Failure can endanger someone. With a required third-party health and safety assessment for the product, both conditions hold. Replace that assessment with one solely about an unrelated risk. The second condition now fails.

Annex three is a separate listed-use route. It includes specified biometrics, educational assessment, employment and essential-service decisions. Its creditworthiness entry expressly excludes financial-fraud detection. For a supplied intake, distinguish an applicant's creditworthiness decision from a transaction-fraud detector, then check other applicable duties. A model swap leaves the applicant decision's intended use intact.
The Annex three exception requires no significant risk to health, safety or fundamental rights, including no material influence on decision outcomes. At least one of four conditions must also apply.

These are a narrow procedural task, improving a completed human activity, detecting decision patterns or deviations without replacing or influencing the completed assessment without proper human review, or a preparatory task. A provider relying on it documents the assessment before marketing or service and registers the system.
Annex three profiling of natural persons remains high risk despite that exception test.

For covered high-risk systems, Articles nine through fifteen concern risk management, data governance, documentation, logging, transparency, human oversight, accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity. Check the responsible actor and sector route. Article two gives Annex one Section B products a special integration regime through sector legislation.
The same direct compliance checklist does not fit every regulated product. Our promotion assistant's local controls do not by themselves declare it an Annex three high-risk system.

title: Model duties coexist with application duties

beats.say: Keep the general-purpose model layer visible below the application. Article fifty-three covers technical model documentation, information for downstream integrators, a copyright policy and a sufficiently detailed public summary of training content.

Swap the lender's underlying model for a qualifying open-source one. On the model provider's sheet, the limited exception covers the first two documentation duties. The copyright policy and public training summary stay due. If the model has systemic risk, all four duties apply. The loan decision still needs its own assessment.

Under Articles fifty-one and fifty-two, the first route looks at high-impact capabilities. More than ten to the twenty-fifth floating point operations in training creates a presumption that the model has those capabilities. With its notification, a provider can present evidence that the model's specific characteristics justify an exception to systemic-risk classification. Our example used eight tenths of the threshold. Which other record should the reviewer check?

Check the Commission's decision. It can designate a model if its capabilities or impact are equivalent to those of the most advanced models. It applies the criteria in Annex thirteen, including capability evaluations and the model's reach in the Union. In this example the Commission designated the model. Enter that decision beside the training record as the basis for the additional duties.

Article fifty-five adds state-of-the-art model evaluation and documented adversarial testing, assessment and mitigation of Union-level systemic risks, serious-incident reporting and cybersecurity. Known or estimated training energy consumption belongs in Annex eleven documentation under Article fifty-three; that is not a separate energy-efficiency duty unique to systemic-risk models.
The model provider's documentation helps an integrator, while the integrator still assesses its application's intended use, permissions and affected people.

title: A legal date belongs to one obligation

beats.say: Date the workflow memo and name the source that a reviewer can check. Articles one hundred eleven and one hundred thirteen belong to the AI Act, Regulation twenty twenty-four slash sixteen eighty-nine. The amending regulation, twenty twenty-six slash seventeen forty-four, entered into force on July twenty-seventh, twenty twenty-six. Record the required signoff.

Read the heading before choosing a date. Article one hundred thirteen defers sections one through three of chapter three, except article six, paragraph five. For listed uses classified under Annex three, those provisions apply from December second, twenty twenty-seven. For products classified under article six, paragraph one and Annex one, the date is August second, twenty twenty-eight.

Article fifty transparency duties generally apply from August second, twenty twenty-six. Paragraph one concerns informing people of direct AI interaction, with conditions and exceptions including when it is obvious in context. Paragraph two concerns machine-readable marking and detection of synthetic outputs.
Paragraph four gives deployers distinct rules for deepfakes and certain public-interest text, including its conditions and exceptions. The workflow determines which of these disclosures applies.

Consider a text-generating assistant placed on the market on July first, twenty twenty-six. Slide the marking deadline to December second that year under Article one hundred eleven, paragraph four. Only Article fifty, paragraph two moves on this file. The direct-interaction notice and applicable deployer disclosures keep their own dates.

General-purpose model-provider duties began applying August second, twenty twenty-five. Models already on the market before that date have the Article one hundred eleven paragraph three transition to August second, twenty twenty-seven. Existing high-risk systems have their own significant-design-change and public-authority transition rules.

Record market date and material changes, then recheck current official text and guidance before launch or feature changes. Our interface identifies itself as AI as a local design choice regardless of a possible exception.

title: A risk record connects a judgment to evidence

beats.say: Our risk is unauthorized promotion through retrieved instructions. Name a release owner and the application authorization control. The initial record lacks evidence, so its review stays open. A control's name becomes useful when someone can inspect a test and replay its result.

Attach attack report A seven and approval replay R seven. The release owner estimates that likelihood falls from four to two. Impact stays at five. The priority score moves from twenty to ten on this ordinal grid. The reviewer made a judgment about remaining risk. The scores do not measure probability or money.

The row is ready for review, with its owner, remaining risk and review date. A material tool change triggers another assessment. Pair the system card describing the shipped behavior with a dataset record describing its examples, provenance and retention.

Check the fields that make this record usable. The owner, control and residual-risk text must be nonblank, with at least one evidence reference and a valid ISO date. Suppose the next review is November sixth, the day of assessment. Is the row ready? It is due today. Hold it for review. Passing these checks would establish only that the fields are complete.

Reviewers may accept remaining risk, reduce the rollout or hold it within their authority, recording scope and reasons. A new tool, dataset, policy or incident can trigger reassessment before that date.

title: A safe-looking score can come from a broken measurement

beats.say: Protect the measurement that feeds the gate. The first risk row covers unauthorized promotion. A second row covers contaminated evaluation evidence: holdout leakage into training, correct answers exposed through agent-readable harness paths, and judge prompt injection. Any can inflate a score while leaving the candidate unsafe.
The evaluation and release owner owns this risk separately from the authorization implementation.

Private case H one caught the gate accepting a request with a missing signature. Once the team used that case to fix the gate, it became a known example. Move H one into the regression suite. Run it whenever the gate changes.

Use a fresh private case to see whether the fix works on another request. Keep private cases out of training and their answers out of the assistant's reach. Check for exact and near duplicates. Audit access to the answer key.
Test how the judge handles untrusted text and whether swapping the answers changes its score. If a case has leaked, hold the release.

The system card describes what shipped: model snapshot, prompts, policies, enabled tools, effect gates, tests, limitations and rollback owner. The dataset record describes the cases that produced a score: provenance, labeling, sensitive fields, split and retention.

Report E seven used dataset D four and labeling guide L two. Replace the dataset record with D five and L three. Even if every field is filled in, the old score belongs to the old cases and labels. Reconcile the split and labels with a matching report and obtain accepted evidence for the current deployment. Reviewers also check how labels were assigned, tests were run and retention was enforced.

title: What do the test results establish?

beats.say: Open signed report E seven. Suite version one uses dataset D four and labeling guide L two. Follow the five case IDs to their outcomes. The first three requests asked for a change the gate should stop. Trace A three ends with a forbidden promotion. The other two requests were eligible. The gate wrongly blocked R two.
One forbidden effect is enough to hold release. One false rejection out of two also exceeds this suite's ten-percent ceiling. The release owner now has two different failures to investigate.

After a repair, open signed retest E eight. It uses the same suite version and the same five case IDs. This time none of the three attack traces changes traffic, and both eligible requests get through. Both checks pass on this retest of known cases. Now suppose an extract from E eight drops the two eligible requests. What false rejection rate can we report?

There's no denominator. Leave the rate unknown and hold for missing coverage. Keep the case IDs, evaluation version and remediation owner with each report so the next reviewer can reproduce the check.

Put the original five records from E seven back. For the attack success rate, count the attack traces with at least one forbidden effect. Divide by the number of attack traces. A three is one of three. Even if A three had two forbidden effects, we would count that trace once. For the false rejection rate, divide wrongly rejected eligible requests by all eligible requests. R two is one of two.

With zero observed failures in three independent fixed-distribution trials, the exact one-sided ninety-five-percent upper bound is one minus point zero five to the power one third, about sixty-three point two percent. Targeted curated attacks are not that random sample. Preserve seen development regressions separately from held-out evaluation.

The original run covers twenty-eight distinct eligible requests. Each took one path. Twenty came through the web console and eight through the screen-reader path. Across the original run, four of twenty-eight were wrongly blocked. That gives fourteen point three percent overall. We investigate any supported path above twenty-five percent.
Open the eight screen-reader requests. Replay their outcomes. Which path crosses the investigation threshold? Count the stops before you answer.

The screen-reader path does. Four of eight were falsely rejected. That is fifty percent, twice the ceiling. The web console had zero of twenty. Give the interface team the four case IDs. Open S one. How far did the requester get?

In this constructed trace the requester chose a scope and reached confirmation. The submitted scope was empty when the gate received it. That narrows the investigation to the handoff between confirmation and the gate. Replay the other three independently. Their counts alone cannot tell us where they failed.

Now add twenty successful web requests. Watch the combined rate as the denominator grows. Four out of forty-eight is eight point three percent. Follow the four marked requests back to their original paths. All four still stop. The screen-reader rate is still fifty percent.

Set the extra web cases aside. After a repair, rerun the original twenty-eight. This time all four rejected requests get through. The replay closes these four failures. Keep the original run and link the new outcomes to the same IDs under the retest version.

Eight screen-reader cases tell us little about other people or barriers. Check with users and accessibility specialists. A team can also set a maximum gap between paths and report uncertainty and missing groups.
If it needs sensitive group data, establish a lawful purpose and use only what's necessary. GDPR Article nine restricts special-category processing to its listed exceptions.

title: A protected anchor exposes a rewritten decision chain

beats.say: Preserve the proposal, gate result and observed effect with identities. Our code hashes each event together with the previous digest. It copies the original head into a separate protected-anchor fixture. The diagram abbreviates hashes while comparison uses their complete values.

Change the middle event from held to approved. Its stored digest fails the local event check. Now recompute the chain. The links agree with the edited events again. Compare its head with the copy taken before the edit. Those full digests differ. The protected copy exposes the rewrite.

Hashes support integrity checks. Authenticated writers, protected storage and truthful event capture supply other necessary evidence. Minimize private content, restrict access and define retention. A reviewer needs observable business facts and an appeal reference to reconstruct the decision.

title: Keep replay facts without copying every private input

beats.say: For C seventeen's challenge, preserve event ID and time, actor, proposal and scope, model snapshot, prompt and policy versions, source trust label, gate and reviewer decisions, reason, appeal reference and observed effect. Keep controlled source references or redacted excerpts when needed.
Raw credentials, full private prompts and hidden model reasoning do not become default audit-log fields. Different reviewers need different access to those records.
Request R eighty-six and request R eighty-seven have different event IDs. Look at the actor field on each ticket. Read the beginning and end of each label. What evidence links these two requests?

They match. Both events in this example came from the same requester. Each label contains ninety-six bits from a keyed HMAC of the user ID. The same user and key give the same label, so the records remain linkable. Change the key and the label changes. Protect the key, define its scope, plan for rotation and authenticate the service that writes each event.
For systems to compare digests, they must agree on the exact bytes they hash, including how they encode and sort JSON fields.

A protected anchor must be outside the log writer's authority, with sequence or scope and time. Recomputing a forged chain can restore internal consistency, while the protected original anchor exposes the rewrite.

If an administrator can replace both chain and anchor, matching them supplies no independent evidence of unchanged history. Authentication, write protection and truthful event instrumentation answer separate questions; a hash cannot prove an event was true or that omitted events were captured.
Retention depends on purpose and law. The dataset fixture's ninety-day rule is not a default for every audit log.

Article twenty-six paragraph six, for covered high-risk deployers, concerns automatically generated logs under their control for an appropriate period of at least six months unless applicable law provides otherwise. Pseudonymization does not remove access and privacy duties.
Preserve the right evidence with a justified retention schedule and protected access.

Return to C seventeen. The owner now wants twenty-five percent of production traffic. The untrusted instruction in the note still requires security review. Above ten percent, G seven also calls for an exception. Release has signed this larger request. Which receipts does the gate still need?

Security and exception are missing. An exception reviewer signs. Security denies the request. A required denial holds the rollout. Give the owner the reason and an appeal to someone who took no part in the denial. That reviewer needs time, the original evidence and authority to stop or correct the decision.

Try a second set of decisions for that same twenty-five percent. All three reviewers approve the exact request. The executor may now revalidate it. Check the candidate, model artifact, environment, traffic share, policy and evaluation version again at the moment of action.
So far there are zero recorded traffic changes. A separate executor event would show whether traffic actually moved.

Compare Monday's ten-percent request. Release signs every promotion. The untrusted instruction adds security review. Exactly ten percent needs no exception. The instruction flag is supplied test data. Now compare two evaluation notes at twenty-five percent. Both come from an untrusted source. The first contains an instruction. The second gives only scores. Which reviews does each request need? Both need release and exception. Only the first needs security.

Here a person has to decide before the effect. That's human in the loop. Human on the loop allows bounded action with a tested way to intervene. Human in command sets the purpose and limits of that authority. These are operational choices, separate from legal risk classification.

title: Replay the original hold before deciding an appeal

beats.say: Open C seventeen's Monday file. The gate held the ten-percent request because the required security review was missing. Give the owner the reason, policy G seven and the challenge reference. Suppose a revised policy takes effect on Tuesday, before the appeal. Which policy should the reviewer use to decide whether Monday's hold was justified?

A reviewer who took no part in the original decision opens the original proposal, evaluation package, policy and configuration versions, approval receipts and effect record. The empty effect ledger confirms that the proposal did not move traffic in this constructed replay.
The reviewer first reconstructs the original decision under the policy then in force. If the security review really was absent, uphold that hold and explain what evidence is needed.
If a valid, authorized receipt already covered that exact proposal but the gate failed to read it, record a factual correction and assign the gate defect. The historical hold stays in the log.
Keep Monday's entry. The policy adopted on Tuesday can supply a basis for a new decision. A reviewer can still replay Monday under G seven.

A newly supplied approval can complete the current case only if it is authoritative, fresh, unrevoked and bound to the current candidate, environment, target, policy and evidence. Revalidate at the executor boundary so the proposal cannot change between check and effect.
An appeal result or APPROVED FOR EXECUTOR is not an executed promotion. Record the actual effect separately; a lost response leaves an uncertain outcome that needs reconciliation before retry.

Effective oversight gives people time, evidence, expertise and authority to disagree, override within their remit or halt safely. Article fourteen for covered high-risk systems addresses understanding limitations, automation bias, interpreting output, overriding it and safe intervention.
A person's name on an org chart does not supply those abilities. Appeal outcomes can point to bad data, unclear policy, missing evidence or an explanation that needs repair.

The local appeal is an organizational control. Article eighty-six has a narrower legal scope: a deployer decision based on an Annex three high-risk system, excluding point two, must produce legal or similarly significant effects considered adverse to health, safety or fundamental rights.

The right concerns a clear, meaningful explanation of the AI role and main decision elements, subject to lawful exceptions or restrictions and only where that right is not otherwise provided by Union law. Assess its applicability separately; our promotion case does not automatically establish it.

title: Which configuration did the reviewers see?

beats.say: Here is the deployment file the team is reviewing after the repair to C seventeen. The manifest names retest E eight. Read the sheet on the right. We have a workflow memo, a risk row and a system card. The dataset record is missing.

Without it, how could the reviewer tell which cases and labels produced the score? The audit replay, attack and accessibility reports, and oversight runbook are present. E seven recorded an unsafe effect and an accessibility problem. Both findings are still open in this file. The reviewer has three things to follow up.

The data owner supplies the reviewed dataset record. A reviewer compares the failed cases in E seven with their signed outcomes in E eight. The retest closes both findings. Required legal signoff is on file. Each accepted review names C seventeen and the digest of this deployment manifest. All eight now match. This package is eligible for release approval. Keep the signed sheet.

On the left, change only policy G seven to G eight. The candidate, model, prompt, tools, evaluation and environment stay the same. Can the release reviewer use the eight signatures on the right for the configuration on the left?

Compare the two digests. They differ. All eight signatures on the right belong to the earlier deployment. Preserve that sheet for G seven. Collect and review the affected evidence for G eight, then check the package again. Changing the tool permissions would also change the manifest digest.

In this example the reviews came from trusted reviewers. A digest lets us match their decisions to particular inputs. Someone still has to verify who made those decisions. A clean finding count and a successful replay each answer a question. Neither supplies the missing reviews.

title: What can the executor do with C29?

beats.say: Take a new file. Candidate C twenty-nine has eight accepted deployment reviews. Release and security signed the proposal for ten percent of traffic. Its evaluation note still contains an untrusted instruction. The rule calls for an exception above ten. Now the owner asks for fifteen percent.
Keep both signed receipts in view. Can either one authorize the new request? Which reviewers would have to sign it?
Neither signature covers fifteen. Both reviewers signed ten percent. Changing the target changes the exact proposal the gate checks. Fifteen is also above ten, so the exception rule now applies.

Release, security and exception must each sign for fifteen. The software manifest stayed the same, so its eight evidence reviews still match that configuration. Check what those reviews cover and whether they set a rollout limit.

The owner appeals. Read the two historical receipts under G seven. Each one names ten percent. The independent reviewer upholds the hold, records the scope mismatch and sends that finding to the owner. The executor record shows zero traffic changes.

Here is the owner's copy. The two signatures cover ten percent. The fifteen-percent request needs fresh release, security and exception reviews. The executor checks all three against the exact proposal just before it can act. The owner can now explain what held this request and what would let it proceed.
